newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends lower, erasing early gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends lower, erasing early gains.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Wednesday, erasing early gains despite stronger physical power and natural gas futures prices.
"It seemed to be oscillating back and forth," said an East Coast electricity broker.

California-Oregon Border (COB) futures remained pressured by growing concerns over ample hydroelectric supplies well into the spring after recent heavy snow and rain in the Northwest and northern California.
"There's a lot more hydro available in California than last year," a Houston futures trader.
The bearish sentiment spilled over to the Palo Verde (PV) half of the complex despite frigid temperatures covering New Mexico and eastern Arizona, market sources said.
"It's a seller's market. People are unwinding positions," the broker said.
February COB futures settled down 16 cents at $14.71 a megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a session high of $15.00. March COB fell 55 cents, closing at $13.30.
February PV futures finished down 30 cents at $16.83/MWh, erasing 12 cent gain. March PV ended down 10 cents at $15.70.
February Henry Hub natgas futures finished up 17.9 cents at $3.513 per million British thermal units.
February gas deliveries at the San Juan/Blanco Hub in New Mexico were last quoted near $3.15/mmBtu, up slightly from Tuesday's $3.05-$3.10 range.
"A lot of people are not bullish on gas in the West," the Houston trader said.
